texts.preamble: Minali Parida vs Kiran Kumar on 27 February, 2017 In The Court Of The Xxii Additional Small Causes Judge And Xx Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate & M.A.C.T., Bengaluru (Scch-24). Present: Smt. Zaibunnisa. B.Com.LL.B. Xxii A.S.C.J. & Xx A.C.M.M. & Member Mact, Bengaluru. Dated: This the 27th day of February, 2017 M.V.C.No.2964/2015 Petitioners : 1. Minali Parida, W/o Narayan Parida, Aged about 41 years, 2. Biswajit Parida, S/o Late Narayana Parida, 25 years, 3. Ranjit Parida, S/o Late Narayana Parida, All resident of Sain Village, Bartana- G.P. Town, Khaira P.S. Balasore District. (Reptd By : Smt. Asha A., Advocate, Bengaluru). - Versus - 2 Scch-24 Mvc No.2964/2015 Respondent: - Kiran Kumar, S/o Kumaraswamy B., Aged about 26 years, R/at No.23, B. Channapura, Bommanayakanahalli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District. And Minali Parida vs Kiran Kumar on 27 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90583259/ 1
texts.facts: 2. The case of the petitioners are as under : The 1st petitioner is the wife and 2nd and 3rd petitioners are the sons of deceased Narayan Parida. That on 15.05.2015 at about 10.30 a.m., near Pizza Hut, G.B. Palya, Hosur Main Road, when the deceased was about to cross the road, a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JD-5532 came rashly and negligently without caring for human safety and dashed against the deceased. Due to impact the deceased fell down and sustained blood injuries all over the body and died on the spot. Postmortem was conducted at NIMHANS, thereafter the body was handed over to the petitioners for 4 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 performing the last rites and the petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards the transportation of dead body and performing last rites. 3. It is submitted that, the deceased was hale and healthy before his death, working as an Assistant Supervisor in G4S Secure Solution (India) Pvt. Ltd., and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. He had very good future prospects and his salary would also rise. Further submitted that, the deceased is only the bread earner in the family and all the family members depends on him for their Minali Parida vs Kiran Kumar on 27 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90583259/ 2 food, clothing and shelter. Due to the accident, the petitioners have lost the earnings of the deceased and the 1st petitioner has lost her loving husband and the 2nd and 3rd petitioners have lost their caring and supportive father and they have put into great agony, pain, frustration and deep mental stress. The complaint has been lodged in the Madiwala Traffic police 5 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 Station in their Crime No.77/2015 for the offences punishable under section 279, 304(A) of IPC against the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-D-5532. The respondent who is the owner of the said vehicle is liable to pay the compensation. Hence, the petitioners pray to award the compensation with interest at the rate of 12% per annum. 4. After service of notice, the respondent has not appeared before this Tribunal. Hence respondent has been placed Ex-parte. 5. On the basis of the above pleadings of the petitioners, the following points arises for my consideration :- POINTS 1. 6 . In order to substantiate the case made out by the petitioners, the 2nd petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and one witness has been examined as P.W.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16. Thereafter, the petitioners closed their side evidence. The petitioners are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.11,36,548/-.
texts.arguments: In the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 1403 between Rajesh and others V/s. Rajbir Singh and others. Wherein it is held that : "Quantum-Fatal accident- Principles of assessment - Future prospects- Whether formula for increase of income for future prospects adopted for person with permanent jobs in Sarla Verma's case 2009 ACJ 1298(SC) may also be applied to 15 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 persons who were self employed or were engaged on fixed wages - Held : yes : 50 percent of actual income (after deduction of tax) for persons below 40 years 30 percent for the age group of 40 to 50 years. 15 percent for age group of 50 to 60 years; but no addition thereafter".
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: In the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 1403 between Rajesh and others V/s. Rajbir Singh and others. Wherein it is held that : "Quantum-Fatal accident- Principles of assessment - Future prospects- Whether formula for increase of income for future prospects adopted for person with permanent jobs in Sarla Verma's case 2009 ACJ 1298(SC) may also be applied to 15 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 persons who were self employed or were engaged on fixed wages - Held : yes : 50 percent of actual income (after deduction of tax) for persons below 40 years 30 percent for the age group of 40 to 50 years. 15 percent for age group of 50 to 60 years; but no addition thereafter".
